function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal authorization that gives a third party (often a bank or payment service provider) the right to act on your behalf. In the context of the API you’re looking at, a mandate typically refers to a *payment mandate*—for example, a SEPA Direct Debit mandate in Europe or a similar authorization in other regions. ### Key points about a mandate | Aspect | What it means | |--------|---------------| | **Purpose** | Allows a merchant, service provider, or partner to initiate payments from a customer’s account without needing the customer to sign each transaction individually. | | **Legal basis** | Usually a signed agreement (paper or electronic) that complies with local regulations (e.g., PSD2 in the EU). | | **Lifecycle** | • **Created** – when the customer signs the mandate.
• **Active** – the mandate is valid and can be used.
• **Pending** – awaiting confirmation or activation.
• **Inactive/Cancelled** – no longer valid (customer revoked or expired). | | **Information stored** | • Mandate ID
• Customer name & account details
• Status (active, pending, inactive)
• Creation and expiry dates
• Signature details (if applicable) | | **Use cases** | • Recurring bill payments (subscriptions, utilities, etc.)
• One‑off direct debits (e.g., a single purchase that requires a debit from the customer’s account)
• Authorizing a partner to collect funds on behalf of a client | ### Why the API exposes mandates - **Partner integration**: Partners (e.g., fintechs, marketplaces) can query the mandates they have on file for their clients. - **Compliance**: By retrieving the status and details of mandates, partners can ensure they only attempt payments on active mandates, reducing failed transactions and regulatory risk. - **Transparency**: Clients can see which mandates exist, their status, and when they expire. ### Quick example of how you might use the API ```python # Fetch all active mandates for a specific client mandates = user_mandates(name="John Doe", status="active") # Or fetch all mandates (any status) for a partner all_mandates = partner_mandates() ``` If you need more detail on a particular type of mandate (e.g., SEPA Direct Debit vs. ACH in the U.S.), let me know!
